chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad Abu Abdullah al-Barqi, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadl, from Thalabah ibn Maymun, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Men are of three kinds: a man (known) by his wealth, a man by his status/prestige, and a man by his tongue. And that is the best of the three.
ai.seo_question: What are the three types of men according to Imam al-Sadiq and which is considered best?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to highlight the Shia ethical hierarchy where internal substance, manifested through speech, outweighs external markers like wealth or lineage. This classification underscores the principle that a person's true worth is determined by their ability to articulate wisdom and truth, a virtue highly prized in Imami scholarship as the primary vehicle for conveying divine guidance.
